PullRequest.Title: chat: count Copilot built-in tools in the Tools badge
PullRequest.Body:

## Problem

In Chat Customizations, the **Tools** badge in the sidebar didn't match what the Tools page shows. The Built-in Tools group includes a read-only **Copilot** tool set (the Copilot CLI's 17 built-in tools, which are always enabled). That set was created privately inside `ToolsListWidget`. The badge counts only used `ILanguageModelToolsService.toolSets`, so those tools were never counted.

## Fix

- Move the Copilot built-in tool set into a shared module, `agentHost/copilotCliBuiltinToolSet.ts`. Add `getCustomizationToolSets()`, which returns the registered tool sets plus the Copilot set.
- Use it for both the Tools page and every badge count:
  - the sidebar of the customizations editor (`ToolsListWidget`)
  - the Agents window customizations toolbar (`readCustomizationCount`)
  - the Agents window customizations overview view

The badge still counts **enabled individual tools**. Tools from Connected Sources (MCP servers and plugins) are still not counted, because their tool lists load only after a server is ready and its row is expanded.

## How to test

1. Open Chat Customizations → Tools.
2. Add up the enabled counts (`n/m`) of the tool sets shown, including the Copilot set's 17 tools.
3. The sidebar **Tools** badge should equal that total. In the Agents window, the toolbar and overview counts should match too.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostToolSetEnablementService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/toolsListWidget.test.ts`: passed (22 tests). Includes a new regression test; two toolbar tests were updated to expect the Copilot tools in the count.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed files. One unrelated error (`setParentWindow` missing on `IPty` in `terminalProcess.ts`), most likely because the local worktree's `node_modules` is out of date.
- Not exercised in a running build.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or search Chat Customizations → Tools and update tool enablement badges
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial render synchronously materializes the registered tool-set iterable, lazily creates the cached 17-tool Copilot set once, enumerates tool memberships for the view model and badge, and renders the tree. Search recomputes the view model after the existing 200 ms delayer; the badge autorun is not dependent on the search query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List tools exposed by a connected MCP server via server.listTools()
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight/load result per ready expanded server until the per-server cache is invalidated; effective count is the number of expanded connected servers, not registered customization tool sets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same expansion-gated listTools call and per-server cache existed before the diff; the new helper neither invokes it nor changes expansion or invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocks population of an expanded connected-server row; it is not on the registered-set badge or Copilot-set construction path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered tool sets and their in-memory member tools; the diff adds one fixed set with 17 members and one shallow array materialization per reactive recomputation. Connected-source tools are excluded from this count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tool-set enumeration and counting are synchronous and serial. Existing connected-source list operations may run once per expanded ready server, potentially concurrently across expanded servers, but this scheduling is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Copilot set and its 17 tool objects are lazily initialized and cached module-wide. Registered tool sets remain observable. Connected tools retain the existing per-server cache and are loaded only after expansion; session changes invalidate that cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper implementation, reactive dependencies, tool-set getTools implementation, search debounce, singleton cache, and connected-tool path were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact extension-contributed set/tool cardinality varies, but the incremental work is fixed at 17 tool checks plus a shallow set-array copy and does not cross an expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff replaces equivalent prior static-set rendering and adds a small fixed in-memory count to badges; it does not increase boundary calls or create unbounded work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and reactively update the Agents window Customizations Tools toolbar badge and total count
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toolbar rendering and subsequent tool-set or enablement observable changes synchronously call readCustomizationCount, shallow-copy registered sets, append the cached Copilot set, enumerate enabled tool IDs, and update the badge DOM.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered in-memory tool sets and member tools, plus the fixed 17 Copilot members. Effective deduplication is by tool ID in countEnabledCustomizationTools.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous autorun; no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The static Copilot tool objects are shared through a module singleton. Observable tool-set and enablement state drive recomputation; no miss/retry behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both the toolbar autorun and count helper were traced to in-memory observable sets and context-key checks only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The registered collection may vary with installed extensions, but the PR's incremental cardinality is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added badge accuracy costs one fixed 17-item scan and shallow iterable copy per relevant observable update, with no hot input/frame trigger or expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display the AI Customizations overview counts in the sidebar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: loadCounts performs the existing prompt/customization discovery first; after it resolves, the tools autorun synchronously computes the badge from registered sets plus the cached 17-tool Copilot set and updates six count elements. Tool-set or enablement changes rerun only that in-memory autorun.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover agent skills and list prompt files and agent instruction files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three parallel section branches per loadCounts call, with the instructions branch performing its existing additional instruction-file listing; cardinality scales with workspace prompt/instruction files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery calls, Promise.all grouping, event triggers, and placement before the tools autorun existed before the diff; adding the Copilot set does not add or repeat any filesystem call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These reads must complete before loadCounts installs/updates the reactive counts, including the tools autorun.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace prompt files for the pre-existing discovery phase; registered tool sets and members for the tools badge, with a fixed 17-member increment from this diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing agent, skill, and instruction discovery branches run through Promise.all; instruction discovery contains a sequential second read. The added tool count is synchronous and serial after discovery and adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-service caching is outside the changed path. The new Copilot set is lazily cached module-wide; each count uses the existing observable tool-set state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: loadCounts ordering and all changed/transitive calls were inspected; no new boundary is reachable from getCustomizationToolSets.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace file-discovery duration varies, but that cost and its triggers are unchanged. The changed work is a fixed in-memory 17-tool count after the existing await.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR does not move or multiply filesystem discovery and adds only bounded in-memory work to the existing tools count.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and relevant reactive callers. The shared helper lazily caches a fixed 17-tool set; badge call sites add a shallow iterable copy and fixed tool scan. Existing filesystem discovery and connected-server tool listing remain unchanged and off the new helper path, so no actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
